ownRead.statement:
## Authoritative core

See **00_LOCKED_CORE.md**. No research example or mathematical model may redefine those terms without passing **05_CHANGE_CONTROL.md**.

## Conceptually locked

1. \(R=(G,M)\): resonant geometry is geometry + full temporal mode structure.
2. \(G\leftrightarrow M\): geometry supports/constrains mode structure; mode structure supports/maintains/transforms geometry.
3. Stability is that self-consistent closure for however long it exists; it is not permanence.
4. Higher structures may contain identical or different lower structures.
5. Lower-level dynamics remain active inside higher levels.
6. Different arrangements/compositions can create different higher resonant geometries.
7. Each scale may use different microscopic mechanisms and equations.
8. Replication is one possible mechanism, not a universal mandatory step.

## Open extensions to prove — not definitions

1. Whether the four known fundamental interactions are manifestations of deeper scale-dependent resonant geometry.
2. Whether gravity is an emergent higher-scale geometric/mode regime.
3. Whether cosmological background evolution selects which resonant geometries are accessible.
4. Whether one cross-domain mathematical invariant or promotion criterion exists.
5. Whether RRG yields a novel prediction beyond existing frameworks.
6. Whether an RRG-inspired AI architecture gives measurable efficiency/generalization advantages.

## Research discipline

New evidence must be used in this order:

\[
\boxed{\text{test locked core}\rightarrow\text{support / extension / contradiction candidate}}
\]

Never:

\[
\boxed{\text{new example}\rightarrow\text{silent new definition}}
\]

A core change requires the complete proof gate in **05_CHANGE_CONTROL.md**.\n\n## Evidence update: emergent interaction channels\n\nAdditional physics evidence supports the mechanism that a lower-level organized medium can generate a higher-level effective interaction:\n\n- phonons mediating effective electron attraction in superconductivity;\n- spin-ice geometry producing emergent magnetic charges with Coulomb-like interactions;\n- the Higgs-field background changing the observable electroweak interaction regime.\n\nThis strengthens the downstream extension:\n\n\\[\nR_n\\rightarrow\\mathcal I_{n+1}^{\\rm eff}\\rightarrow R_{n+1}.\n\\]\n\nIt does **not** close the claim that the four fundamental forces themselves are all deeper RRG manifestations.\n

ownRead.statement:
This file tells us what must be proved **without changing the locked core**.

| Claim | Status | What would count as evidence | What would count against it | Core impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Geometry constrains supported modes | supported in many known systems | spectral/normal-mode calculations and experiments | a claimed application where geometry has no definable mode relation | none unless it contradicts locked definition |
| Modes can maintain/transform geometry | supported in many systems | backreaction, coupled-mode, optomechanical, self-organization examples | failure in a specific implementation | none |
| Heterogeneous lower structures can form a higher resonant geometry | core claim / common in known systems | molecules, cells, composite systems, network modes | genuine contradiction must pass change-control proof gate | possible core impact only after proof gate |
| Lower-level modes remain active inside higher structures | core claim | multiscale measurements/reductions | evidence that higher formation literally eliminates lower state variables in a claimed case | proof gate required |
| Different scales may use different mechanisms | locked | established effective theories already allow this | no issue | none |
| Same equation family reappears at each scale | optional strong extension | RG fixed points/universality/form-invariant reductions | different effective equations across scales | rejects extension only |
| Four forces are deeper resonant-geometry manifestations | open extension | derivation of known interactions/charges/ranges/symmetries from a deeper model | incompatibility with observed force structure | extension rejected; core unchanged |
| Gravity is emergent resonant geometry | open extension | recover equivalence principle, Lorentz/diffeomorphism structure, GR limits | experimental/theoretical no-go under model assumptions | extension rejected; core unchanged |
| Cosmic background selects accessible geometries | open extension | derive/fit known phase transitions and structure windows | model fails while standard physics succeeds | extension rejected/refined |
| Cross-domain RRG invariant exists | open extension | same measurable criterion predicts organization in ≥2 unrelated domains | criterion becomes domain-specific or post-hoc | extension weakened |
| RRG improves AI | open application | controlled benchmark gains at equal resources | no gain / worse scaling | application rejected; core unchanged |

| Lower-level organization can generate an effective higher-level interaction channel | supported in known physical systems | phonon-mediated attraction, emergent spin-ice charges/interactions, collective mediated interactions | a claimed system where the proposed emergent interaction cannot be derived or measured | supports extension; core unchanged |

## Rule

A failed extension is **not** permission to redefine the core. It is simply a failed extension unless a complete core contradiction passes `05_CHANGE_CONTROL.md`.

## 1. Geometry \(G\)

In RRG, **geometry** means the organization of a system at a chosen scale:

\[
G=\{\text{components, arrangement, relations, connectivity, order, orientation, boundaries, constraints}\}.
\]

Geometry is not limited to visible Euclidean shape.
ownRead.plainLanguage: Organization at a chosen scale includes components, relationships, boundaries and constraints.
ownRead.scope: A locked RRG meaning; a definition is not an experimental finding.

decisions.rationale: Full mode structure and explanation preserve phase, amplitude, coupling, response and timescales; a single hertz value is not a unique geometry.

ownRead.statement:
## 2. Frequency / mode structure \(M\)

In RRG, **frequency** is shorthand for the system's full temporal mode organization, not one scalar value in hertz:

\[
M=\{\omega,\phi,A,\psi,\text{propagation, coupling, characteristic timescales, response}\}.
\]

A scalar frequency alone is never assumed to uniquely determine a geometry.
ownRead.plainLanguage: Mode structure includes rhythms, phases, coupling, response and characteristic times, rather than one number in hertz.
ownRead.scope: A locked RRG meaning; a definition is not an experimental finding.

decisions.rationale: Pair and reciprocal relation preserve neither-side-universally-first; source structural interpretation, not a cross-domain theorem.

ownRead.statement:
## 3. Resonant geometry \(R\)

The basic RRG object is:

\[
\boxed{R=(G,M)}.
\]

Geometry and mode structure are inseparable aspects of one organized system:

\[
\boxed{G\leftrightarrow M}.
\]

- Geometry constrains/supports which modes can exist.
- The active mode structure supports, maintains, transforms, or destroys the geometry.

Neither side is defined as universally "first".
ownRead.plainLanguage: RRG considers organization and mode structure together. Each constrains or changes the other.
ownRead.scope: A locked RRG meaning; a definition is not an experimental finding.

ownRead.statement:
## 4. Stability

**Locked definition:** a geometry is stable in RRG while its geometry and mode structure form a self-consistent closed organization:

\[
\boxed{G\leftrightarrow M}.
\]

Stability is **not permanence**. A state may satisfy the closure for a very short or very long interval.

Lifetime, perturbation recovery, Lyapunov stability, decay width, or metastability are **measurements/tests of a particular system**, not replacements for this core definition.
ownRead.plainLanguage: RRG calls the geometry–mode organization stable while it is self-consistent. This does not require permanence.
ownRead.scope: A locked RRG meaning; a definition is not an experimental finding.

ownRead.statement:
## 7. Scale

A **scale** is a level at which a collective resonant geometry can function as an effective unit in further interactions.

Different scales may have different:

- characteristic sizes,
- characteristic times/frequencies,
- dominant interactions,
- effective mechanisms,
- compositions and geometries.

RRG does **not** require the same microscopic mechanism or identical equation at every scale.
ownRead.plainLanguage: A collective organization can function as an effective unit in further interactions. Mechanisms may differ across scales.
ownRead.scope: A locked RRG meaning; a definition is not an experimental finding.

decisions.rationale: Conditional higher-level formation and explanation preserve heterogeneous compatible members and retained internal activity; no prior-duplication requirement.

ownRead.statement:
## 5. Higher-level formation

A higher-level resonant geometry may be formed from any compatible collection of lower-level resonant geometries:

\[
\boxed{\{R_n^1,R_n^2,\ldots,R_n^m\}\rightarrow R_{n+1}}.
\]

The lower-level members:

- do not need to be identical;
- do not need to duplicate first;
- can have different roles and internal modes;
- remain internally active after the higher-level structure forms.

The higher level introduces new collective constraints and a new collective mode structure while containing the lower levels.
ownRead.plainLanguage: Compatible lower-level systems may form a higher-level organization while retaining internal activity. Their components may differ.
ownRead.scope: A locked RRG meaning; a definition is not an experimental finding.

decisions.rationale: Variation and explanation preserve differing organization and conditions without adding a physical selection law.

## 6. Variation

Different counts, arrangements, compositions, orientations, connections, phases, and environments may create different higher-level resonant geometries from the same lower-level building blocks.

\[
\boxed{\text{same or related lower units}+\text{different organization}\rightarrow\text{different }R_{n+1}}.
\]

Variation is therefore fully compatible with the core and requires no new principle.
ownRead.plainLanguage: Related building blocks can participate in different organizations under different arrangements and conditions.
ownRead.scope: A locked RRG meaning; a definition is not an experimental finding.

ownRead.statement:
## 8. Recursion

The core recursive claim is structural:

\[
\boxed{\{R_n^i\}\rightarrow R_{n+1}\rightarrow R_{n+2}\rightarrow\cdots}.
\]

At every level the locked relation remains:

\[
\boxed{R_n=(G_n,M_n),\qquad G_n\leftrightarrow M_n}.
\]

The mechanisms implementing the relation may change with scale.
ownRead.plainLanguage: Organized units may take part in further organization. This structural claim does not require an identical microscopic equation.
ownRead.scope: A locked RRG meaning; a definition is not an experimental finding.

decisions.rationale: Replication and explanation preserve an optional mechanism rather than a mandatory step at every level.

ownRead.statement:
## 9. Replication / recurrence

Replication, duplication, autocatalysis, reproduction, aggregation, differentiation, self-assembly, and symmetry breaking are **possible mechanisms of higher-level formation or propagation**, not mandatory steps in the core recursion.

RRG never requires:

\[
A\rightarrow A+A\rightarrow B
\]

at every level.

Biological replication is therefore an example, not the definition of recursion.
ownRead.plainLanguage: Replication is one possible way to form or propagate organization; it is not required at every level.

## 10. Interaction / force status

The following is **NOT locked as established fact**:

> known forces are identical to resonant frequencies or correspond one-to-one with scales.

The locked core only says that interactions occur within and between resonant geometries and can participate in forming higher-level geometries.

The stronger claim that gravity, electromagnetism, weak, and strong interactions are scale-dependent manifestations of deeper resonant geometry is an **RRG extension to be proven**, not a definition.

ownRead.statement:
## 1. Phonon-mediated effective attraction in superconductivity

In conventional superconductivity, electrons couple to lattice vibrations (phonons).

At the microscopic level, electrons and ions interact electromagnetically. The organized crystal lattice, however, possesses collective vibrational modes. Electron–phonon coupling can generate an **effective electron–electron attraction** in the appropriate regime, allowing Cooper pairing and superconducting order.

\[
\boxed{
\text{crystal geometry}
\rightarrow
\text{phonon modes}
\rightarrow
\text{effective electron interaction}
\rightarrow
\text{Cooper pairing / superconducting order}
}
\]

The effective attraction does not replace electromagnetism as a fundamental interaction. It is a higher-level interaction generated through collective lattice dynamics.

### RRG relevance

This directly supports the extension:

\[
G_n \leftrightarrow M_n
\rightarrow
\mathcal I^{\rm eff}_{n+1}
\rightarrow
G_{n+1}.
\]

### Evidence

X. H. Zheng & D. G. Walmsley, *Physical Review B* 71, 134512 (2005).  
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.71.134512

## 2. Emergent magnetic charges and Coulomb-like interactions in spin ice

Spin-ice materials contain microscopic magnetic moments constrained by lattice geometry and frustration.

Collective correlations in this many-body geometry permit excitations that behave as **emergent magnetic monopoles** rather than elementary magnetic charges.

Castelnovo, Moessner & Sondhi predicted these quasiparticles as emergent manifestations of the correlated spin-ice system.

Bramwell and collaborators later experimentally measured effective magnetic charges and currents in Dy\(_2\)Ti\(_2\)O\(_7\), showing that these emergent charges interact through a Coulomb potential.

\[
\boxed{
\text{microscopic spins}
+
\text{collective geometric constraints}
\rightarrow
\text{emergent quasiparticles}
+
\text{Coulomb-like effective interaction}
}
\]

### RRG relevance

This demonstrates that a collective geometry can generate:

- new effective particle-like degrees of freedom;
- a higher-level interaction law;
- behavior that is not apparent from treating each microscopic spin independently.

### Evidence

Castelnovo, Moessner & Sondhi, *Nature* 451, 42–45 (2008).  
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06433

Bramwell et al., *Nature* 461, 956–959 (2009).  
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/nature08500

Mengotti et al., *Nature Physics* 7, 68–74 (2011).  
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys1794

ownRead.body:
A wave is a pattern in moving water. A molecule has connected atoms. A living cell exchanges material while maintaining an organization.

Unity Theory asks how **arrangement and activity work together**—and how an organized whole can become part of something further.

## Begin with a wave

Look at a ripple crossing water. The pattern travels, while the water moves locally. The parts and the collective pattern give us two ways to describe what is happening.

This is a warm-up for the question, not evidence that every wave becomes a persistent building block.

## Arrangement shapes activity. Activity changes arrangement.

The research framework calls these two aspects **geometry** and **mode structure**. Geometry includes relationships, connections, boundaries and constraints. Mode structure includes patterns of change, coupling, response and characteristic times—not just a single frequency.

An organized whole may then act as a component of another system, while activity continues inside its parts.

ownRead.body:
## Start with parts and relationships

Think of a stretched string. Its length, material, tension and fixed ends constrain how it can move. Change those conditions and the possible motions change too. Shape alone does not explain the result: material properties and physical interactions matter.

Recursive Resonant Geometry, or **RRG**, uses “geometry” for a system's organization at a chosen scale. That includes its components, connections, relationships, boundaries and constraints. It means more than a visible outline.

## Add what happens over time

The second aspect is **mode structure**: the organized ways a system can change, respond or move. This includes characteristic times, phases, coupling and collective activity. A single number in hertz does not describe all of it.

RRG treats organization and mode structure as two aspects of one system. Organization constrains activity; activity can support, maintain, transform or destroy organization. Neither is universally first.

This is the framework's proposed way of describing a system. Whether a particular model makes useful predictions requires separate tests.

## A whole can become a part

A molecule can participate in a larger arrangement. A cell can participate in a tissue. In the RRG framework, compatible lower-level systems may form a higher-level organization while retaining their internal activity. The components can differ and play different roles.

“Recursive” describes that possibility of organized wholes participating in further organization. It does not mean every system must copy itself, or that every scale must obey the same microscopic equation.

## Existing organization can change the possibilities

The question also concerns the environment: an existing organization may change the conditions under which further organization becomes possible. This is an extension to investigate, rather than a guarantee that complexity must increase.

The current research also asks when lower-level organization generates or enables an **effective interaction**—an interaction useful in a higher-level description—that could help another organized state persist. The evidence documents discuss specific physical systems. Those examples do not derive all four fundamental forces from RRG.

## What the examples do—and what remains open

These examples introduce relationships the project investigates. Different systems have different mechanisms and conditions; an analogy does not demonstrate a universal law.

The current sources distinguish core definitions from extensions, candidate mathematical models and evidence in particular systems. Open work includes a useful cross-domain criterion and novel predictions beyond existing frameworks. The technical website sections will make those distinctions visible alongside their sources.

[Return to the research question](/#research-question).
